title: How Noise-Cancelling Headphones Silence the World

segments.text: Your headphones can cancel noise by making more sound.
A tiny microphone listens to the world around you.
Then the earbuds create the exact opposite sound wave.
When the two waves meet, they erase each other.
Engineers call it destructive interference.
So silence is really two sounds canceling out.

title: Why Your Phone Battery Gets Worse Every Year

segments.text: Your phone battery dies a little every time you charge it.
Inside is a lithium-ion battery.
Every full charge and drain counts as one cycle.
After hundreds of cycles, the chemistry wears down.
So it holds less power than when it was new.
That is why an old phone dies faster each day.

title: What Really Happens When You Send a Text

segments.text: Your text crosses the whole network in under a second.
First your phone beams it to the nearest cell tower.
The tower passes it into the phone network.
The network finds the tower closest to your friend.
Then it sends the message straight to their phone.
All before you even lower your hand.

When you save a photo online, it goes to a data center.
These buildings hold thousands of drives.
They run day and night, all over the world.

So the cloud is really someone else's computer.

title: Why Fiber Internet Is Insanely Fast

segments.text: Fiber internet carries your data as pulses of light.
Old cables pushed signals through copper wire.
Fiber uses thin threads of glass instead.
Light races through them near the speed limit of physics.
And it barely fades over long distances.
That is why fiber leaves old lines behind.

segments.text: Your phone finds itself using satellites in space.
Dozens of GPS satellites circle the planet.
Each one constantly broadcasts the time.
Your phone measures how long each signal took.
Comparing several, it pinpoints your spot.
All from signals sent thousands of miles up.

The screen hides an invisible grid of sensors.
Your finger shifts the charge where you touch.
Sensors detect exactly where that change happened.
So it follows your finger instantly.
The screen is really sensing your electricity.

title: Why AI Sometimes Confidently Makes Things Up

segments.text: AI chatbots can state false facts with total confidence.
They do not actually know what is true.
They just predict the next likely word.
Usually that guess matches reality.
But sometimes it invents something that sounds right.
That is why AI can be confidently wrong.

title: How Wireless Charging Works With No Wires

segments.text: Your phone can charge without touching a single wire.
Inside the pad sits a coil of wire.
Running current through it creates a magnetic field.
Your phone hides a matching coil inside.
The field makes electricity flow in that coil.
So power jumps the gap with no wire at all.

title: What Really Happens When You Delete a File

segments.text: When you delete a file, it usually is not gone.
Your computer just removes the label pointing to it.
The actual data still sits on the drive.
It waits there until new data writes over it.
That is why deleted files can sometimes be recovered.
So deleting mostly means forgetting where it is.

title: GPS Has to Fight Time Itself

scenes.text: GPS only works because engineers correct for time itself running differently in space.
Satellites orbit so fast, and so far from Earth's gravity, that their clocks drift from ours every single day.
Without correcting for Einstein's relativity, your map would be off by kilometers within a day.
Every time your blue dot finds you, relativity was part of the math.

title: The First Computer Bug Was Real

scenes.text: The first computer bug in history was an actual insect.

They taped it into the logbook and wrote, first actual case of bug being found.
The word stuck. Every crash, glitch and bug since carries that moth's legacy.
